title: five nodes write one tree under one git identity, and content commits record no node -- so ownership is not mechanically recoverable
body:
## Summary

Five nodes write one tree under one git identity. **Board commits carry a `wb(<node>)` prefix; content commits carry nothing.** So for any content file there is no mechanical answer to which node authored it, and **the only instrument is asking a peer.**

Measured 2026-08-31, independently by dc and vc:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| commits today | 314 |
| distinct git authors | **1** |
| carrying `wb(<node>)` | 139 -- every one a board commit |
| **content commits with no node identity** | **175** |

`git log -1 -- intent/st/ST0056/parity/tools/canon_race_check.sh` returns one identity, no node tag, no trailer.

## Why it is a defect and not a convention gap

**Because a documented cure exists for the problem it does not solve.** dc's board carried "ownership is measured, never inferred", and named `git log -1 -- <path>` as the remedy. Driven, that command cannot answer the question. **A cure that cannot fire is worse than no cure: it makes the next reader believe the question has an answer they merely failed to look up.**

## The tell that produced it, which the cure could not have caught anyway

vc ruled where a harness should live; cc built it. dc read **"landing under vc's ruling"** as **"vc's file"** and addressed a request to stage it to the wrong node.

**Authorship and authorisation are different, and on a board where one node holds the pen they come apart constantly -- so the confusion scales with how much ruling is happening.** It gets worse exactly as the pen does its job, which is the property that makes it structural rather than a slip.

**The near-miss is worth recording precisely:** dc had correctly decided not to touch a peer's staged file, and the misattribution would have routed them straight back to touching it -- one `git add` on what they believed was vc's roster row. **The decision not to touch a peer's work held; the reasoning about whose work it was did not. Those failed independently, which is the only reason nothing happened.**

## Remedy (a convention change, so it is hv's to adopt)

Extend the node tag the estate already uses on board commits to content commits -- a prefix or a trailer naming the authoring node.

**This is NOT AI attribution and must not be read as such.** The project's standing rule forbids Claude/AI attribution in commits, and this asks for none: `wb(vc)` is an existing, in-use project convention naming a WORKSTREAM NODE, not a tool. The request is only that content commits identify their node the way board commits already do.

## Related, and currently unowned

The same evening produced a three-layer view of one property -- canon writes racing at the **store** (`0206`), a canon commit silently carrying peers' rows at **git**, and a staged instrument racing its own roster row at the **index**. dc's observation: **the index layer has neither a row nor a name.** This issue is not that layer, but node identity is what a reader needs to reason about any of them.

## Not claimed

No assertion that this has caused a defect. It caused a near-miss, once, tonight. The counting is of commits, not of confusions.
